proof_assessments.reason: For a fixed linear part q, E_J has additive translation fiber u_J(q)+K_J. Quotienting by a Q-invariant translation subgroup M changes this to (u_J(q)+K_J+M)/M. Two such fibers meet exactly when the lift difference belongs to K_J+K_T+M, and a nonempty intersection is a coset of ((K_J+M) intersect (K_T+M))/M. For q in Q_C an actual E_C lift is a common representative; hence equality of kernel lattices gives precisely its E_C/M fiber. For q outside Q_C the exclusion condition is necessary and sufficient. Conversely the identity fiber forces the kernel equality and every outside fiber must be empty. All lattices contain M, so quotient equality lifts to subgroup equality. Changing representatives changes a difference only by K_J+K_T. This argument covers arbitrary rank M, including zero; no finite-index assumption is used.
proof_assessments.computability: AL.1 uses normalized Schreier translations to compute exact K_J from finite Q_J. Integer lattice sums, intersections and membership give a finite procedure for a fixed finitely generated M. Neither this algorithm nor the reviewer samples establishes a uniform parameter theorem.
proof_assessments.attribution: Classical additive-coset intersection formula; the common arbitrary-parabolic formulation is new to this edition, without a historical priority claim.
proof_assessments.formal_status: Not formalized by the inherited faithful-parabolic period certificates.

proof_assessments.reason: The surjection from the actual abstract kernel Z^d onto the rank-d lattice L is injective, so the presented affine base is E, not merely a group with an affine quotient. Invariance makes the additive span of the period-basis words equal to their normal closure. The general period criterion then supplies IP for B. The finite antichain, stated deletions and injectivity on proper local marked subgroups are exactly the supported-kernel hypotheses. The four explicit presentation conditions supply the relator map, local maps, normality and exact base quotient required by UA.Recognition; its separate coordinate maps exclude any remaining kernel. Thus the full compatible product and all parabolic coordinate kernels follow. The finite order formulas use exact kernels and the base index. The geometric/Helly and deletion conclusions retain their extra hypotheses; they do not follow from IP alone.
proof_assessments.limits: Exact base recognition and the source-specific normality/relator checks remain obligations. Classification, forest converse and census are not reduced to this construction theorem.

proof_assessments.reason: Faithfulness of the two adjacent linear images sets both relevant translation kernels to zero; the general criterion therefore reduces to the finite common-linear-part exclusion modulo M. The explicit distinct nonidentity involution condition supplies the rank-three criterion, rather than assuming it from the general marking. The exact normal closure, finite index/order and solvability arguments are retained. A solution for every parameter still requires its stated arithmetic proof.

For the indicated support the dihedral covering is faithful on proper marked subgroups and has the required cyclic kernel when the base edge order divides the lifted order. The one-support case of UA.SK supplies generation of the full compatible product, projection kernel and IP. Exact presentation recognition uses all relators, the normal local cyclic kernel and the exact base quotient. It does not rely on comparing finite orders and thus also applies to the infinite base.

The two supports form an antichain. Both local dihedral relations hold. The first fourth-power cyclic subgroup is inverted by its two local generators and centralized by the third; the corresponding statements hold separately for the second subgroup. Thus each is normal in the whole presented group. Every source relator holds in the compatible product, and killing the two fourth powers gives exactly the previously identified square period presentation. These are all four recognition hypotheses; no order bound is used in place of presentation injectivity. The exact order and solvability then follow from the identified base and cyclic kernels.

The fourth-power kernel is normal by inversion and the specified centralization. Killing it gives the complete infinite affine presentation. The retained relations hold in the base and have trivial dihedral coordinate, so recognition applies before any finite periods are imposed. The source period words are the retained explicit vectors; their normal closure is exactly the invariant translation lattice with trivial local coordinate. The original parity and literal sign correction are preserved. No finite quotient is used as proof of the infinite base presentation.
